summary: Daniel Sperber is a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Kol Torah, Kilburn Grammar School, Yeshivah of Flatbush, and University College London (~1965–1968). He held posts at Bar-Ilan University (from ~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper, Jr. specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Veidlinger specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Nalini Devdas, Samli Mulkæo, and Steven Collins, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago. He held posts at Chiang Mai University (1999) and California State University, Chico (attested 2006).

Daniel W. Kent works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as an instructor in 2010. He also held an instructor post at Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).

Daniela Berti works in Indology and religious studies. She earned a PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology from the University of Siena and was a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya (attested 2004).

Daniela Bevilacqua works in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from the University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University. She held a post as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
Daniele Cuneo held academic posts at the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (both attested 2018). He taught Arinde L. Jonker.
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst. She also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.

Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937), later serving as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1953–1992).

Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Hindu College, University of Delhi (~1957–1960), University of Delhi (~1960–1966), Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1974–1976).

Daud Ali is an Indologist and historian. Educated at William & Mary and the University of Chicago (MA, PhD under Ronald Inden), he taught history at SOAS University of London (~1995–2005) before joining the University of Pennsylvania as associate professor in 2009.
David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968), and held an academic post at Stony Brook University from around 1970.

David A. Hall specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima (1976) and completed his doctorate at UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the doctoral supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He held posts at Rice University and Santa Clara University (attested 2005–2017).

David Brainerd Spooner was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Stanford University (~1895–1899). He served as Directeur p. i. du Service archéologique de l’Inde at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1906–1925).

David Brick is an Indology scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle (attested 2009). He served as a professor at Yale University (attested 2012–2018) and on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (attested 2012).

David Brown worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied under Joseph Milner (~1778–1782) and at Magdalene College (1782). He served as Provost at Fort William College (~1800–1806) and founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society.

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD at Western Sydney University and served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) and held positions at Keble College (attested 2001) and Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).
